💡 The novelty lies in a trace-metal-assisted flash (TMF) process that uses in situ nickel nanoclusters to catalyze ultrafast graphitization of amorphous carbon into highly ordered graphite in under one second. This yields fast-charging graphite anodes with superior rate capability and cyclability, while cutting energy use, emissions, and production cost by over 80%, offering a scalable, sustainable route for next-generation lithium-ion batteries.

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in constructing an amorphous lithium reservoir (ALR) of short-chained lithium polysulfides on sulfur particles, creating disordered Li─S bonding that stores and anchors Li⁺, enabling fast Li⁺ conduction and continuous supply for accelerated S/Li₂S conversion. This resolves sluggish triple-phase interfacial kinetics, yielding high-power, energy-dense all-solid-state Li─S batteries (1115 mAh g⁻¹ at 1C, 12.8 mAh cm⁻² at 10 mg cm⁻² loading).

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using solvation entropy engineering to create a high-entropy deep eutectic solvent that tunes ligand accessibility and competitive metal-ligand interactions, enabling universal selective Ni recovery from diverse spent NCM cathodes. Its significance is establishing solvent microenvironment engineering as a complementary design principle to ligand engineering for selective metal separation in complex multimetal systems.

Nature Sustainability | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty is an O6-type layered Li-rich cathode formed by atomic-scale O3/O1 intergrowth, which suppresses transition-metal migration and irreversible oxygen dimerization. Its significance lies in stabilizing oxygen-redox activity, enabling negligible voltage decay and high energy-density retention in a cobalt-free cathode, establishing stacking-sequence design as a general strategy for durable sustainable batteries.

Chemical Society Reviews | 💭 Perspective | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in transferring lithium battery design heuristics to aqueous electrolytes, revealing that optimal transport rules differ fundamentally from nonaqueous systems. This is significant because it challenges prevailing assumptions, provides new design principles for aqueous batteries, and could accelerate development of safer, lower-cost energy storage.
